Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profiles. We are trying to nail down budgeting and want to understand Redwood's baseline hosted API pricing and how volume discounts kick in.

Quick context: FastCommerce will move its checkout recommendation engine to an LLM-backed reranker. We expect a bursty profile with estimated 2B tokens/month initially, growing to ~7–8B tokens/month by Q4 with occasional spikes. We are evaluating both pay-as-you-go and committed-commit options.

Questions:
- What are your published per-token rates for hosted text generation and embeddings?
- Do you offer step-down discounts at specific breakpoints (monthly committed tokens)?
- Any one-time onboarding or reserved-capacity fees we should budget for?
- If we commit to a 12-month consumption band, what kind of credits or true-up mechanics do you offer?

Hi Claire — great to meet you and glad the demo was useful. Appreciate the forecast — that helps a lot. High level answers below, then I included a few concrete scenarios based on your numbers.

Baseline (hosted API) starting points
- Text generation: $0.0008 / 1K tokens (base public rate for smaller consumption)
- High-throughput slab (unadvertised entry points): step discounts begin at 500M tokens/month
- Embeddings: $0.0012 / 1K tokens (varies by model)

Volume/Committed options (examples)
- Pay-as-you-go: no minimum, billed monthly at baseline rates. Good for early experimentation.
- Committed monthly bands (12-month term): 3 tiers we typically use for customers of your scale:
  * Tier A: 1–2B tokens/mo — 10% credit on monthly invoice (effective rate ~ $0.00072 / 1K)
  * Tier B: 2–5B tokens/mo — 18% credit (effective rate ~ $0.000656 / 1K)
  * Tier C: 5B+ tokens/mo — 28% credit and access to dedicated pool slots (effective rate ~ $0.000576 / 1K)

Other notes:
- Onboarding: no mandatory setup fee for hosted; professional services for integration charged separately.
- True-ups: we support quarterly true-ups for committed bands; overages billed at the baseline rate without a penalty tier.

Scenario pricing (based on your forecast):
- Month 1 (2B tokens): Tier B gives meaningful savings compared to pay-as-you-go (estimate attached).
- Q4 peak (8B tokens): Tier C with burst credits and dedicated pool is the most predictable economically — we can structure a blended effective rate if you prefer smoothing across months.

I attached a rough ratecard (proposed_ratecard_v2.pdf) and a simple spreadsheet modeling the three-tier commitment. If it looks close, I can loop in Ben on the commercial side to discuss contract mechanics and if we can offer an introductory uplift credit for a 12-month commit.

Available times: Tue/Wed next week for a short pricing sync?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
